intro: These are add-ons, not requirements. A leader can substitute one for a weekly challenge, add one to a month, or let the group choose one together. The goal is embodied faithfulness, not competition.

physical.text: One week with no sugary drinks
One week of drinking water consistently
Take the stairs whenever practical for one week

spiritual.text: 24-hour fast from food or a normal meal pattern, as appropriate
Pray for one person every day for a week
Read one Gospel in a month
Spend one hour in extended prayer

relational.text: Write a letter of gratitude to your wife or a friend
Ask forgiveness from someone you have wronged
Have a phone-free meal with your family
Invite a newer man into a meal or activity

missional.text: Pray with someone outside your immediate family
Share your testimony with another person
Serve someone who cannot repay you
Invite a man into a Scripture conversation

guardrails: Physical challenges should build stewardship and brotherhood, not shame. Men should scale challenges to their age, fitness, injuries, health, and season of life. No man should feel pressured to compete, disclose health information, or attempt an activity that is unsafe for him.
